scope: Primary Intel interrupt/READY ordering and current vm80a adapter source; no physical origin or replay qualification
supported_physical_ordering: INT is asynchronously presented; acceptance requires INTE high and phi2 in the last state of the completing instruction.
Figure2-8 illustrates internal request storage during the phi2 high interval; it does not support treating the MAME opcode callback as a pin edge.
The following interrupt M1 presents status INTA/D0 with SYNC; PC is presented but not incremented; externally supplied instruction is received during T3.
READY is checked during phi2 of T2/TW; exit from TW requires READY setup before phi2 falling, then advances at the next phi1 rise.

current_vm80a_equations.interrupt_input: on enabled master edges with f2: intr<=pin_int
current_vm80a_equations.last_state_bridge: on f2: mstart<=~ms0 & ~ms1; on f1: inta<=1 when irq & ((tw & sy_hlta)|(mstart & ~id_eidi))
current_vm80a_equations.priority: later f1 clear wins if ~intr | id_eidi | (t5 & id_rst)
current_vm80a_equations.enable: on f2: t1f1 & id_eidi writes inte=i[3]; t1f1 & sy_inta clears inte
current_vm80a_equations.ready: ready=pin_ready|((m4|m5)&id_dad); f2 chooses TW or T3 from T2f1/TWf1
current_vm80a_equations.phase_gates: f1 phase0..4; f2 phase8..19; phase wraps24->0; all donor sequential storage shares !pause CE

field66_source_projection.interpretation: The request precedes the source-model final ANA phi2 gate closure; following phi1 qualifies interrupt start. This preserves the existing explanation and negative, rather than establishing absolute PCB phase.
